title: Faithful-flat comparison of model fibre stalks and descent of a regular singleton
statement: Let $A_0\to A$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, $B_0$ a commutative $A_0$-algebra, $B$ a commutative $A$-algebra, and $e:A\otimes_{A_0}B_0\xrightarrow{\sim}B$ an $A$-algebra isomorphism [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Let $\mathfrak q\subset B$ be prime, $\mathfrak p\subset A$ its contraction, $\mathfrak q_0\subset B_0$ its contraction under $b_0\mapsto e(1\otimes b_0)$, and $\mathfrak p_0\subset A_0$ the common contraction. Put $k_0=\kappa(\mathfrak p_0)$, $k=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, $E_0=B_0\otimes_{A_0}k_0$, and $E=B\otimes_A k$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. There is a canonical $k$-algebra isomorphism $E_0\otimes_{k_0}k\cong E$ induced by $e$. For the fibre prime $\mathfrak r\subset E$ corresponding to $\mathfrak q$ and its contraction $\mathfrak r_0\subset E_0$, it induces a faithfully flat local homomorphism $C_0=(E_0)_{\mathfrak r_0}\to C=E_{\mathfrak r}$ [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map]. The canonical identifications $C_0\cong(B_0)_{\mathfrak q_0}/\mathfrak p_0(B_0)_{\mathfrak q_0}$ and $C\cong B_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak pB_{\mathfrak q}$ commute with the map from $B_0$. If $a_0\in B_0$, $a=e(1\otimes a_0)\in\mathfrak q$, and multiplication by the image of $a$ in $C$ is injective, then the singleton consisting of the image of $a_0$ is a regular sequence in $C_0$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]; in particular that image lies in the maximal ideal, is a nonzerodivisor, and has nonzero quotient.

source.place: Tag 056Y, label lemma-slice-given-element, proof, second paragraph: residue-field base change of fibre local rings and faithful-flat descent of the chosen nonzerodivisor (old steps 6–7).

proof.text: Write $f:A_0\to A$ and $i:B_0\to B$, $i(b_0)=e(1\otimes b_0)$. The equality $f^{-1}(\mathfrak p)=\mathfrak p_0$ defines a field map $u:k_0\to k$: it sends the residue class of $x/s$ to that of $f(x)/f(s)$. Denominators remain outside $\mathfrak p$, and elements of $\mathfrak p_0$ map to zero; conversely a numerator maps into $\mathfrak p$ exactly when it belongs to $\mathfrak p_0$. Thus the fraction formula is well defined and injective, and $k/k_0$ is a field extension.

source.place: Tag 056Y, lemma-slice-given-element, proof second paragraph, fibre-local-ring comparison and descent of the nonzerodivisor; expanded using Algebra Tags 00E6, 0H9M, 00HI, 00HT, 00HR and 05CK.

proof.text: The tensor universal property gives $\Phi:(B_0\otimes_{A_0}k_0)\otimes_{k_0}k\to B\otimes_Ak$ by $(b_0\otimes\lambda_0)\otimes\lambda\mapsto i(b_0)\otimes u(\lambda_0)\lambda$. For the inverse, first replace $B$ by $A\otimes_{A_0}B_0$ using $e^{-1}$, and send $(t\otimes b_0)\otimes\lambda$ to $(b_0\otimes1)\otimes\bar t\lambda$, where $\bar t$ is the image of $t\in A$ in $k$. The balancing relations over $A_0,A,k_0$ make both formulas well defined; their composites fix pure tensors. Both preserve products and the $k$-action. This proves the asserted canonical $k$-algebra isomorphism and identifies $E_0\to E$ with $z\mapsto\Phi(z\otimes1)$.

source.place: Tag 056Y, lemma-slice-given-element, proof second paragraph, fibre-local-ring comparison and descent of the nonzerodivisor; expanded using Algebra Tags 00E6, 0H9M, 00HI, 00HT, 00HR and 05CK.

proof.text: The fibre-localization quotient formula writes every element of $E$ as the class of $b/f_A(s)$ with $b\in B$, $s\in A\setminus\mathfrak p$, where $f_A:A\to B$ is the structure map. The map $E\to\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ sends this fraction to the corresponding residue fraction. Its kernel $\mathfrak r$ is prime and membership is equivalent to $b\in\mathfrak q$, since $f_A(s)\notin\mathfrak q$. This also proves uniqueness of a prime contracting to $\mathfrak q$. Its contraction $\mathfrak r_0$ along $E_0\to E$ contracts to $i^{-1}(\mathfrak q)=\mathfrak q_0$ in $B_0$; the identical fraction test for $B_0,A_0$ makes it the fibre prime corresponding to $\mathfrak q_0$.

source.place: Tag 056Y, lemma-slice-given-element, proof second paragraph, fibre-local-ring comparison and descent of the nonzerodivisor; expanded using Algebra Tags 00E6, 0H9M, 00HI, 00HT, 00HR and 05CK.

proof.text: Apply faithful flatness of field-extension base change with $K=k_0$, $K'=k$ and $D=E_0$. Step 2 identifies its map $E_0\to E_0\otimes_{k_0}k$ with $E_0\to E$, so the latter is faithfully flat and hence flat. The flat-local-ring-map lemma at $\mathfrak r$ and its contraction $\mathfrak r_0$ now gives the canonical flat local map $\psi:(E_0)_{\mathfrak r_0}\to E_{\mathfrak r}$, sending $z/t$ to its image fraction. The flat-local faithful-flatness lemma applies to these prime localizations and proves $\psi$ faithfully flat.

source.place: Tag 056Y, lemma-slice-given-element, proof second paragraph, fibre-local-ring comparison and descent of the nonzerodivisor; expanded using Algebra Tags 00E6, 0H9M, 00HI, 00HT, 00HR and 05CK.

proof.text: Apply the natural fibre-local-ring isomorphism first to $A\to B,\mathfrak p,\mathfrak r$ and then to $A_0\to B_0,\mathfrak p_0,\mathfrak r_0$. It identifies the two local rings with the quotients in the statement and sends the class of $b/s$ to $(b\otimes1)/(s\otimes1)$ in each case. On $b_0\in B_0$ both routes to $C$ therefore give $(i(b_0)\otimes1)/1$. This is the required compatibility with the map from $B_0$; in particular $\psi$ sends the image $\alpha_0$ of $a_0$ to the image $\alpha$ of $a$.

source.place: Tag 056Y, lemma-slice-given-element, proof second paragraph, fibre-local-ring comparison and descent of the nonzerodivisor; expanded using Algebra Tags 00E6, 0H9M, 00HI, 00HT, 00HR and 05CK.

proof.text: Faithfully-flat universal injectivity with $R=C_0$, $S=C$ and $N=C_0$ makes $C_0\to C_0\otimes_{C_0}C$, $x\mapsto x\otimes1$, injective. Under $x\otimes c\mapsto\psi(x)c$ (inverse $c\mapsto1\otimes c$) this is $\psi$. If $\alpha_0x=0$, then $\alpha\psi(x)=0$. Injectivity of multiplication by $\alpha$ gives $\psi(x)=0$, hence $x=0$. Thus $\alpha_0$ is a nonzerodivisor without any Noetherian hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 056Y, lemma-slice-given-element, proof second paragraph, fibre-local-ring comparison and descent of the nonzerodivisor; expanded using Algebra Tags 00E6, 0H9M, 00HI, 00HT, 00HR and 05CK.

proof.text: Since $a=i(a_0)\in\mathfrak q$, we have $a_0\in\mathfrak q_0$ and $a_0\otimes1\in\mathfrak r_0$. Hence $\alpha_0\in\mathfrak r_0C_0$, the maximal ideal of the prime localization $C_0$. The principal ideal $(\alpha_0)$ is contained in that proper ideal, so $1\notin(\alpha_0)$ and $C_0/(\alpha_0)\ne0$. Together with Step 6 this is precisely regularity of the singleton in the stated definition, and establishes every final clause.

Step 6: universal injectivity with N=R=C_0 makes ψ injective, so the nonzerodivisor descends. Step 7: a_0∈q_0 puts α_0 in the maximal ideal r_0C_0, so the quotient is nonzero, and both clauses of def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence hold. Small cases tested: Z→F_p with Z[T] at (T) (a non-flat base), Q→C with a_0=T^2+1 at (T-i), a unit a, a field stalk, k[ε]/(ε²), inseparable k/k_0.
